headline: The USA FREEDOM Act of 2014 would have limited government collection of phone and other records under foreign intelligence surveillance law and added transparency and privacy rules, but the Senate did not advance it.
what_it_does: The bill would have required the FBI to use a specific selection term, such as a named person, account, or device, when asking a secret FISA court for business records, and it would have barred orders that lack one. It would have set stricter rules for collecting call detail records, including a 180-day limit on daily orders and a two-step limit on how far records could be traced. It would also have expanded public reporting on surveillance orders, created special advocates to argue for privacy in FISA court, and extended certain expiring surveillance provisions to December 31, 2017.

who_it_affects.how: They would have been required to provide records under the new selection-term rules, been protected from liability for doing so, and been paid for reasonable expenses, and they could have published aggregate counts of orders they received under set reporting options.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. persons whose call records or communications might be collected
who_it_affects.how: They would have gained limits on collection, rules for destroying irrelevant information, and a bar on using their information without consent except in threat cases.

who_it_affects.group: Federal intelligence and law enforcement agencies such as the FBI and the Department of Justice
who_it_affects.how: They would have had to follow the new selection-term, emergency production, national security letter, and reporting rules, and undergo inspector general audits of 2012 to 2014 activities.

who_it_affects.group: Judges on the FISA court and the FISA court of review
who_it_affects.how: They would have had to appoint special advocates to argue privacy-focused positions in cases involving novel or significant legal questions, unless they found that inappropriate.

who_it_affects.group: Financial institutions and consumer reporting agencies
who_it_affects.how: They would have received national security letter requests that must name a specific person, entity, or account, and they would have been notified when a nondisclosure requirement ended.
